notes: Allow-list of audited brain-decryptd kernel builds. Each entry is a
(version, sha256) tuple; the hash is lowercase hex of the daemon
binary's bytes. Content is deployment-agnostic — same binary has the
same hash on every Mac Mini.
The brain plugin ships this file alongside the validator binaries.
Plugin updates roll out new audited entries automatically (the
validator stores the path, not the content, and re-reads each tick).
Empty 'audited' = enforcement mode but no audited builds yet. The
validator surfaces every trust_kernel_version block as
kernel_unaudited in its status snapshot — a correct strict-defender
signal that the audit ceremony hasn't been performed for the running
build. Populating this array requires an external auditor (or, for
the engineering pilot, manual sign-off) to certify a specific
(version, hash) pair.
Threat model: see
docs/decryptd-protocol-reference.md#threat-model-kernel-version-attestation
in the cortex repo. The on-chain trust_kernel_version block is a
self-attestation; this allow-list defends against operational drift
and server-side allow-list tampering, not against an adversarial
daemon. Admin-on-host `sha256` of the running binary is the
out-of-band ceremony that closes the trust circle.
